Delta State Governor Sheriff Oborevwori has proposed a budget of N1.23tn for the 2027 fiscal year, promising to execute projects within available resources without resorting to borrowing. The governor said his administration would reject any loan facility from the Federal Government but accept grants to support development projects in the state. Oborevwori disclosed this on Monday, November 16, 2026, while presenting the 2027 Appropriation Bill, tagged “Budget of Sustained Prosperity and Enhanced Growth”, to the Delta State House of Assembly. The proposed budget allocates N806.8bn, representing about 65 per cent of the total expenditure, to capital projects, while N420bn, representing about 35 per cent, is earmarked for recurrent expenditure. The governor said the 2027 proposal was a reduction of more than N400bn from the N1.7tn 2026 budget, explaining that the decision was part of efforts to ensure fiscal discipline and spend within the state’s financial capacity. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources He said, “If you look at our 2026 budget, it is N1.7tn, and this 2027 budget is N1.2tn. You can see the difference because we are going to spend within what we have. “If we want to borrow, we will just jack up our budget to N2tn because we are a big state. But we will try as much as possible to do things within our budget and what we are expecting.” He stressed that any financial support from the Federal Government must come in the form of grants. “I don’t like borrowing, and we are turning down any money they are going to give to the state that is for borrowing. But if it is going to be grants, we will take it. For borrowing, we will not take it,” he said. According to him, the 2027 budget is designed to sustain the state’s development drive and improve the welfare of residents, irrespective of the political activities surrounding the election year. “When we talk about 2027, people talk about elections, but the election has nothing to do with the 2027 budget. The budget is for our people,” he said. He added, “In 2027, the election will not affect our budget performance. We will do more because we are injecting more into the system. More things will happen because it is going to be MORE Plus in 2027. On the implementation of the 2026 budget, the governor attributed the pace of capital project execution partly to prolonged rainfall between July and August, saying the administration had achieved about 60 per cent performance. He expressed optimism that capital expenditure would improve before the end of the year, noting that the government was monitoring ongoing projects to ensure proper execution. “Because of the prolonged rain between July and August, we were able to do 60 per cent. We are sure that by the last quarter of the year, we will achieve more on capital projects,” he said. The governor said the administration would continue to monitor contractors and follow up on projects to ensure that allocated funds translated into completed infrastructure. The proposed revenue sources for financing the 2027 budget include internally generated revenue, statutory allocations, mineral resources revenue and Value Added Tax. Efecha Gold
